findings.text: The dispatched done_when requires every one of the five queued dispatches to be under ten seconds; the recorded measure is 29.36, 13.20, 12.94, 13.52 and 14.03 s, so the quantitative clause fails; the worker records the shortfall rather than claiming it met, and the node's remaining deliverable stands. The plan was amended after this node's evidence commit to move the absolute dispatch target into section 21, which is what makes the shortfall non-blocking here, but the goal sentence as dispatched is not achieved: a dispatch still does not answer in ten seconds.

The done_when names a timing measure on the fleet node; the measure ran on the allocation node 98dci4-clu-2001 at load 8.83 to 12.39. The deviation is stated in the fragment, and discovery dominates the result by two orders of magnitude over the fence, so the conclusion holds, but the measure does not satisfy the clause as written.

The new docstring says omitting session keeps the project-wide reading 'the drain asks for', and the test and evidence fragment repeat that two surfaces call this function. No drain calls it: the only production caller at head is reckon/crew/dispatching/fences.py:362 (reached from preparation.py:571 and requests.py:225); the drain reaches the same predicate through _partition_session_rows and its own readers. The optional default is still worth keeping for the exported surface in reckon/crew/recovery.py:439, but the stated reason names a consumer that does not exist.

The ownership test 'no recorded owner stays in scope, otherwise the owner must match the session' is now spelled twice in one function's neighbourhood: inline here before classification, and again in _partition_session_rows at recovery_watch.py:544. The pre-filter cannot call the partition helper because it must run before the read, so the duplication is not avoidable by that route, but the rule now has two spellings that can drift.

VERDICT done_when: read the done_when in dispatch-detail.json and the plan section; the classifier clause (200 peer pointers, none classified) and the 'under half a second per dispatch' clause are met by the 0.04 s scoped and 0.06-0.09 s in-dispatch measurements, while the 'every one is under ten seconds' clause is not met and the 'still refused naming that run' bullet no longer describes the code (backlog recorded, not enforced, settled before this node).
VERDICT write_paths: read the declared scope (reckon, tests, the evidence fragment directory, the figure directory); both commits touch only reckon/crew/dispatching/fences.py, reckon/crew/recovery_watch.py, tests/test_a_dispatch_classifies_only_its_own_runs.py and the fragment under docs/evidence/fragments/queued-work-needs-no-workaround/.
